items.title: El Niño floods kill 34 in Ecuador and swamp Peru's Piura
items.why: Ecuador's risk management agency said on Friday that rains linked to El Niño have killed 34 people and left about 47,000 homeless or affected since late August. In northern Peru, waist-high water filled the streets of Piura after 12 hours of rain, affecting about 2,000 families, civil defence officials say.
items.matters: Forecasters expect this El Niño to be one of the strongest on record, bringing more heavy rain.

items.title: Taiwan votes in local elections and a referendum on nuclear power
items.why: Polls opened on Saturday for about 19.6 million voters to choose more than 11,000 local posts, including mayors of Taiwan's six largest cities. A separate referendum asks whether to drop the 'nuclear-free homeland' policy; Taiwan shut its last reactor in May 2025.
items.matters: Chip and AI factories need more power; the result also tests the parties before the 2028 national elections.

items.title: OpenAI countersues Apple, accusing it of taking trade secrets
items.why: OpenAI filed counterclaims against Apple in a California federal court on Friday, saying Apple took OpenAI secrets through a former employee and pressured shared suppliers to slow its move into devices. Apple, which sued OpenAI earlier this year over alleged theft of its own secrets, calls the countersuit a distraction.
items.matters: The two firms are partners on ChatGPT in iPhones but are becoming rivals in AI-powered gadgets.

items.changed: Updated: an Israeli strike hit a Doctors Without Borders clinic
items.title: Israeli strike on Gaza clinic kills two Doctors Without Borders guards
items.why: Doctors Without Borders (MSF) says an Israeli strike on its clinic in Gaza City on Friday evening killed two of its guards, bringing its staff killed in Gaza to 17. Israel's army says both men were Hamas members. The WHO chief called the attack 'outrageous and unacceptable'.
items.matters: Strikes continue despite the October 2025 ceasefire, and Israel threatens a wider offensive unless Hamas disarms.

items.title: Uganda starts Africa's first mRNA vaccine trial against Ebola strain
items.why: The Uganda Virus Research Institute and Moderna began Africa's first trial of an mRNA vaccine against the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola on Friday. About 224 volunteers aged one to 65 will take part. No vaccine is approved for this strain, which is behind Congo's outbreak.
items.matters: A working vaccine could help stop an outbreak that has killed more than 5,000 people in neighbouring Congo.

items.title: Canada's Supreme Court largely upholds Quebec's religious symbols ban
items.why: Canada's top court on Friday largely upheld Quebec's 2019 secularism law, which bars teachers, police officers and some other public workers from wearing religious symbols at work. Six of seven judges said Quebec lawfully used the Charter's 'notwithstanding clause'; three judges said the law breaches religious freedom.
items.matters: Quebec's premier called it a victory; Muslim and civil liberties groups criticised the ruling and vow to keep challenging it.

items.title: Overton takes five as England bowl Australia out for 108
items.why: Jamie Overton took five wickets for 12 runs as England dismissed Australia for 108, their lowest T20 international total at home, at the Gabba in Brisbane on Friday. England won by seven wickets in a rain-shortened chase to lead the five-match series 2-1.

items.title: Bodies found on migrant boat off Spain's Canary Islands
items.why: Spain's maritime rescue service said eight to ten people were found dead on a boat carrying about 100 people, 72km south of El Hierro, on Friday; Spanish media later reported 14 dead. Six were flown to hospital in serious condition. The boat had left Gambia ten days earlier.
items.matters: Arrivals in the Canary Islands have surged since October, and migration is a key issue in Spain's election on Sunday.

items.title: Kenyan cult leader Paul Mackenzie convicted of manslaughter over 123 deaths
items.why: A court in Mombasa, Kenya, on Friday convicted preacher Paul Mackenzie of manslaughter over the deaths of 123 followers in Shakahola Forest, where he told them to fast to death. He is already serving 200 years for the murder of 191 people, almost all children. His lawyer plans to appeal.
items.matters: Authorities have recovered more than 400 bodies at Shakahola, prompting calls for closer oversight of religious groups.

items.title: UK benefits department takes online services offline after cyber incident
items.why: The UK's Department for Work and Pensions took some online services offline on Friday, including Universal Credit and pension accounts, after finding a cyber incident on Thursday evening. It says payments are not affected but has not said what happened or whether data was taken.
items.matters: The department warns it will never message people asking for bank details or to click links, so watch for scams.

items.title: At least 13 soldiers killed in attack on army post in Niger
items.why: At least 13 National Guard members were killed and 20 wounded in an attack on their post at Sanam in western Niger, near the border with Mali, on Thursday, Niger's defence ministry says. The Islamic State group claimed responsibility, Reuters reports. Two days earlier, 11 soldiers died in the south-east.

items.title: Thanksgiving storm cuts power to 900,000 and delays Macy's parade
items.why: A storm along the US East Coast cut power to more than 900,000 homes and businesses at its peak on Thursday, the Thanksgiving holiday, tracking site poweroutage.us says. New York's Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade was postponed to Saturday, the first weather postponement in its history.

items.title: India's Rishabh Pant plays New Zealand park cricket as 'Stan Stan'
items.why: India wicketkeeper Rishabh Pant joined a social eight-a-side match in Christchurch, New Zealand, on Wednesday as 'Stan Stan', after a local player spotted him on an electric bike and asked him to fill in. He hit a rapid half-century with a borrowed bat; opponents did not recognise him.

items.title: New Zealand's governing coalition falls one seat short in final count
items.why: Final results released on Friday give Prime Minister Christopher Luxon's three-party coalition 65 of 130 seats, one short of a majority, after special votes moved two seats. The centrist Opportunity party, with seven seats, now holds the balance of power.
items.matters: If no deal is reached, New Zealand could face a second election.

items.title: EU leaders end summit without a deal on budget or Ukraine loan
items.why: After more than 12 hours of talks in Brussels on Thursday, EU leaders failed to agree the bloc's 2028-2034 budget or a €45bn loan for Ukraine next year, and cancelled the second day. They will try again on 17-18 December.
items.matters: Ukraine relies on EU money to keep its government running and its army supplied.

items.title: Venezuela to repeal law used to ban opponents from office
items.why: National Assembly leader Jorge Rodríguez said on Thursday that lawmakers will begin repealing the 2024 'Simón Bolívar' law on 1 December. It sets prison terms of up to 30 years and long bans from office for anyone backing foreign sanctions on Venezuela. Rights groups call it a tool against dissent.
items.matters: The move is part of talks between the government and part of the opposition.

items.title: Argentina bans its central bank from printing money for the government
items.why: Argentina's Congress gave final approval on Thursday to a law that makes protecting the peso's value the central bank's main job and bars it from financing the Treasury. The lower house passed it 141 to 0, with 99 abstentions.
items.matters: Printing money to pay government bills helped push Argentina's inflation above 200%; it has since fallen to about 33%.

items.title: Israel's Eisenkot agrees coalition deal with left-wing Democrats
items.why: Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar party and Yair Golan's Democrats announced on Thursday that they had agreed coalition terms, giving the Democrats four ministries. Together with Avigdor Lieberman's Israel Beiteinu they hold 36 of the Knesset's 120 seats; 61 are needed. Eisenkot has until 6 December to form a government.
items.matters: It is the latest step in the attempt to replace caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu after October's inconclusive election.

items.title: Spain's Pablo Hernández de Cos chosen to lead the European Central Bank
items.why: EU leaders meeting in Brussels on Thursday picked Pablo Hernández de Cos, 55, a former Bank of Spain governor, to succeed Christine Lagarde as ECB president. He is due to take over in February and would be the first Spaniard in the job.
items.matters: The ECB sets interest rates for the 20 countries that use the euro, where inflation is about 4%.

items.title: French actor Gérard Depardieu ordered to stand trial for rape
items.why: A Paris appeals court on Thursday upheld an order for Gérard Depardieu, 77, to stand trial over the alleged rape of an actress at his Paris home in 2018, and dismissed a second allegation. Depardieu denies wrongdoing; his lawyer said an appeal to France's highest court is being considered.

items.title: Guinea-Bissau's military rulers delay elections by two years to 2028
items.why: Guinea-Bissau's transitional president, Gen. Horta Inta-a, on Thursday postponed presidential and legislative elections planned for 6 December to November 2028, citing a lack of technical, material and financial means. The army seized power in the West African country a year ago.
items.matters: It extends military rule well beyond the one-year transition promised, despite pressure from West African neighbours.

items.changed: Updated: Italy says the drone was made in Iran
items.title: Two Italian technicians killed in drone attack in Kuwait
items.why: Two Italian technicians working for Rheinmetall Italia died after drones hit an air-defence site in Kuwait on Thursday. Italy's foreign minister, Antonio Tajani, says Kuwaiti investigators found the drone was made in Iran. Iran denies launching it and has offered a joint inquiry.
items.matters: Italy plans a formal complaint to Iran, drawing a European country further into the Gulf conflict.

items.title: Bank of England warns AI borrowing raises financial system risks
items.why: In its twice-yearly Financial Stability Report on Thursday, the Bank of England said AI financing is 'increasingly complex, circular and opaque'. Big AI cloud companies are on course to issue more than $305bn of bonds this year, and share prices still look 'stretched', it says.
items.matters: If expected AI profits do not arrive, losses could spread to banks, pension funds and ordinary savers.

items.title: News agency AFP takes client platform offline after cyber-attack
items.why: France's AFP news agency says hackers got into AFP Forum, the platform clients use to download its stories, photos and videos, from about 1:30am Paris time on Thursday. The platform remains offline. AFP says it does not yet know who is responsible.
items.matters: France's cybersecurity chief says the country faces an 'unprecedented' cyber threat; FIFA also reported a hack that day.

items.title: FIFA confirms hackers took some personal and business information
items.why: Football's world governing body, FIFA, said on Thursday it was the victim of a 'criminal cyber-attack' that gave access to 'a limited set of personal and business information'. It did not say how many people were affected. A hacking group claims to have taken more than 12 gigabytes of files.

items.title: US disables cargo ship near Hormuz as Iran claims tanker mine strikes
items.why: US Central Command says its aircraft disabled the Palau-flagged cargo ship Pacific Archer in the Gulf of Oman on Thursday after it left Iran's Bandar Abbas port; the crew was unharmed. Iran's Revolutionary Guards say tankers hit mines near Hormuz, claims that cannot be verified.
items.matters: Attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz, a key oil route, can push up fuel prices worldwide.
items.changed: Updated: the US says it disabled a ship that left an Iranian port

items.title: UK net migration falls to 77,000, lowest since 1997 outside pandemic
items.why: Net migration to the UK, the number arriving minus the number leaving, fell to an estimated 77,000 in the year to June 2026, the Office for National Statistics said on Thursday. About 738,000 people arrived and 661,000 left. It peaked at more than 900,000 in 2023.
items.matters: Migration has been a central issue in British politics; the government and opposition each claim credit for the fall.

items.title: North Korea has paused military aid to Russia, Ukraine's intelligence says
items.why: Ukraine's military intelligence said on Thursday that Kim Jong Un had suspended deliveries of KN-23 missiles and artillery shells to Russia and barred Russian military planes from North Korean airspace, after a row over Moscow's outreach to South Korea. Neither Moscow nor Pyongyang has commented, and the claim is unverified.
items.matters: North Korea has sent Russia missiles, shells and thousands of troops for its war in Ukraine.

items.title: Ebola outbreak in Congo passes 12,000 confirmed cases
items.why: Congo's government says 12,021 people have been confirmed with Ebola and 5,904 have died since the outbreak was declared in Ituri province in May. The Bundibugyo strain has no approved vaccine or treatment. Fighting near Bunia has forced some health workers to evacuate, the WHO says.
items.matters: Reuters calls it the second-largest Ebola outbreak on record; officials say many infections are going undetected.

items.changed: Updated: China, the EU, Japan and Brazil rejected the plan
items.title: US proposes new tariffs on China, the EU and 12 other economies
items.why: The US trade office proposed import taxes of mostly 10% to 20% on 14 economies, saying they produce far more than they need. On Thursday China said it reserves the right to respond, the EU said the US should respect its trade deal, and Brazil called the plan 'unacceptable'.
items.matters: Tariffs can raise prices for shoppers and hurt exporters; China calls the claims false and the EU rejects them.

items.changed: Updated: the death toll has risen to at least 13
items.title: At least 13 dead as rescuers search flooded Indonesian gold mine
items.why: At least 13 miners have died after an unlicensed gold mine in the Pongkor area of Bogor, West Java, flooded late on Monday, Indonesia's local search and rescue chief says. Thirteen others are still missing, and 11 escaped. About 325 rescuers are working in shafts around 100 metres deep.

items.changed: Updated: the coalition says it struck 50 Houthi targets in Yemen
items.title: Saudi-led coalition strikes Yemen after deadly attack on Jazan refinery
items.why: A projectile hit Saudi Aramco's Jazan refinery on Thursday, killing a Nepali worker, Saudi Arabia's energy ministry says. The Saudi-led coalition blames Yemen's Houthis and says it then destroyed 50 Houthi military targets in Sanaa, Hodeidah and Saada provinces. The Houthis had not commented.
items.matters: Jazan can refine about 400,000 barrels of oil a day, so attacks there can push up fuel prices.
